items.title: Henry A. "Hank" Kmen Interview, 1963-02-13
items.q: Whereas Hutchins Ryder, a clarinet player, was good then and has been good all the way, and sounds remarkably good today.

ctx.x: Pat Davis. Pat Davis. Pat Davis. He was much admired by almost all the saxophone players I knew. In fact, some of them, at one time he used a baritone mouthpiece on a tenor to get a broader sound, and that became a thing a lot of guys did, put a baritone mouthpiece on a tenor. But very soon they came to regard him as nothing. He wasn't really a lasting man or a lasting influence. Whereas Hutchins Ryder, a clarinet player, was good then and has been good all the way, and sounds remarkably good today.

Well, specifically, getting back to what I'm supposed to be researching, I want to get some of your attitudes about early New Orleans musicians that you've heard and have some sort of impression of. You know, whether they were considered corny or good, and how you knew them and why, and just anything.
